overview: The season ended with the Heysel disaster. Before the European Cup final against Juventus in Brussels on 29 May 1985, 39 people, mostly Juventus supporters, died after a wall collapsed following a charge by Liverpool supporters. The final went ahead and Liverpool lost 1–0. English clubs were subsequently banned from European competition.

Liverpool finished second in the First Division, 13 points behind Everton, and lost their FA Cup semi-final replay to Manchester United. Tottenham ended their League Cup run in the third round. There were also defeats by Everton in the Charity Shield, Independiente in the Intercontinental Cup and Juventus in the European Super Cup.

John Wark was leading scorer with 27 competitive goals. Graeme Souness had left for Sampdoria, while Paul Walsh and Jan Mølby joined from Luton and Ajax. Joe Fagan retired at the end of the season; his decision to step down had been made before Heysel.
